home.about_1: What a DAC really accepts (sample rates, native DSD or DoP, what each input lets through) is scattered today across makers' spec sheets, manuals, forums and measurements. Players and listeners alike often have to guess. ODAC gathers these facts in one place, readable by everyone and by software.
home.about_2: Every fact carries its evidence: the source that establishes it, quoted and dated. When two sources disagree, both values stay visible with their weight. When nobody knows yet, the question is asked openly instead of leaving an empty cell.
home.about_3: A record is judged on two separate measures. Identification says whether a player can recognise the device, by its USB identity or by a match established by a person. Completeness says what is known about it: level 2, what it accepts; level 3, what it does inside. Each says what the next contribution would let a player decide.
home.about_4: Like Wikipedia or MusicBrainz, ODAC is a commons: the data is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and the code Apache 2.0. The project is stewarded by Mozaiklabs together with the community, and stays open to any sourced contribution.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.intro: ODAC grows fact by fact, each one with its source. Anyone who owns a device, reads a spec sheet or takes a measurement can help.
contribute.today: Today: a pull request on GitHub
contribute.step_1: Open the ODAC-Project/ODAC repository and read the contribution guide.
contribute.step_2: Add or correct a claim: the fact, the source (address, date read) and an account in which the source’s words that establish it are quoted inside « ».
contribute.step_3: Sign every commit with the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO), that is a “Signed-off-by” line (git commit -s).
contribute.step_4: Open the pull request: the automatic check validates the format, then a curator re-reads the source.
contribute.dco_text: The DCO certifies that you have the right to submit what you propose. It asks for no extra account and no transfer of rights, only your sign-off on each commit.
contribute.soon_text: A form will let you propose a fact without using Git. It is not open yet: until then, GitHub is the only way in.
contribute.rule_1: A source that names this exact model, not just the range.
contribute.rule_2: The source’s words inside « », exact and short (300 characters at most per excerpt): what carries the fact, not the whole table.
contribute.rule_3: “Unknown” is better than a guessed value.

help.title: Help & FAQ
help.intro: Short answers to the most frequent questions.
help.a1: A precise source (spec sheet, manual, measurement, retailer page) with the date it was read, and an account of what it establishes. The source’s own words that carry the fact are quoted inside « », at most 300 characters per excerpt; the rest is written by the contributor. One piece of evidence can establish several fields; the record shows it only once.
help.a2: Two sources give different values for the same field. ODAC does not settle it silently: it shows every value with its weight and says which one the build retained.
help.a3: A question asked publicly about the device that nobody has answered with a source yet. That is often where a measurement or an owner of the device moves the record forward.
help.q4: What do identification and the levels mean?
help.a4: They are two separate measures. A device is identified when a player can recognise it: by an exact USB identity (VID and PID), or by a match established by a person, with its evidence. The levels measure content: level 2 says what it accepts (sample rates, DSD, DoP, inputs), level 3 what it does inside (chip family, DSD conversion, level offset). A record can be complete at level 2 without being identified: it is described, but a player does not yet know it is facing it. Neither measure says anything about quality: every fact present must carry its evidence.
help.q5: Why “to be measured” rather than an empty cell?
help.a5: Because the question has been asked and nobody knows the answer yet. An explicit reason is better than a blank, which could pass for an oversight.
help.a6: The file https://odac.tune.audio/latest.json gives the fingerprint of the current snapshot and the address of the artifact, a JSON Lines file served compressed. Software downloads it only when the fingerprint changes. The details are in CONSUMING.md, in the repository.
help.a7: The facts are licensed CC BY-SA 4.0: you may reuse them by crediting ODAC and sharing alike. Quotations remain the property of their authors. The site's code is licensed Apache 2.0.

path.title: The signal path
path.intro: The sheet read in the order the sound travels through the device. Each step says why a player needs it; a dashed box is a question still open.
path.why_inputs: The inputs and the rate each accepts: a player never sends more than the input in use can take.
path.why_formats: Rate, resolution, native DSD or DoP: without these ceilings a player resamples blindly or sends a stream that is refused.
path.why_conversion: The chip or conversion technology (delta-sigma, R-2R, FPGA) tells which signal it prefers to receive.
path.why_inside: DSD turned back into PCM, PCM remodulated to DSD: if the device already does it, doing it upstream is useless, or harmful.
path.why_output: Analogue filter, PCM/DSD level offset, settings: what a player must compensate so that a format change cannot be heard.

ladder.level2_gives: The player sends the right format, no trial and error.
ladder.level3_gives: The player prepares the signal for this very device.

why.title: Why ODAC
why.intro: An audio player knows almost nothing about the DAC it feeds. ODAC gives it the facts, each with its source, so that it processes the sound upstream the way the device wants.
why.problem: Over USB a DAC announces at best the rates it accepts. It does not say whether it converts DSD directly, remodulates everything internally, or plays DSD louder or quieter than PCM. A player that ignores this picks its settings at random.
why.example_1: A DAC that already oversamples everything has nothing to gain from software upsampling; a non-oversampling R-2R DAC may.
why.example_2: Sending DSD to a device that converts it back to PCM pays the cost of DSD without its benefit.
why.example_3: Many DACs play DSD a few dB lower than PCM. Known, the offset is compensated; unknown, it is heard at every track change.
why.identity_long: An exact USB identity or a sourced match. Without it the other facts are useless: the player does not know which device they apply to.
why.level2_long: The ceilings of each input, the bit depth, native DSD and DoP. The minimum to never send a refused stream.
why.level3_long: The chip, the internal handling of DSD and PCM, the level offset, the filter. What lets processing adapt to the device.
why.rule_1: Every fact has its source: maker's sheet, manual, published measurement, with the date it was read.
why.rule_2: Two sources that disagree both stay visible: the database does not settle silently.
why.rule_3: The database is open (CC BY-SA 4.0): any player can read it, not only Tune.
